heroHeadline: Russia Issues 'Mortal Danger' Warning to Diplomats as Missile Strikes Kill 6 Across Ukraine
heroSubtitle: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones overnight into September 24, killing 2 and injuring 8 and damaging Maternity Hospital No. 2 and the historic 1906 St. Pokrovsky Church, then hit the capital again overnight into September 25 with a mass drone barrage across six districts plus Brovary and Lutsk, killing 7 — including two children — and injuring 59. Ukraine responded on September 25 with long-range drone strikes on the Lukoil oil refinery in Perm (~1,450km inside Russia, 1 killed), the Iskra defense-electronics plant in Ulyanovsk (8 injured) and the Voronezhsintezkauchuk synthetic-rubber and rocket-propellant plant in Voronezh (13 injured); Russia claimed 592 drones intercepted overnight. Separately, Russian drones struck a medical center and ambulances in Zaporizhzhia on September 25, injuring 1. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,525,570 by September 25, per the Ukrainian General Staff. On September 26, Russia's FM Lavrov declared the war would continue 'through to the end,' China unveiled a peace plan signaling a diplomatic posture shift, and Zelensky said Russia shows no readiness to stop as Ukraine and allies plan additional pressure. On October 1, Russia launched its largest combined ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine's energy grid in months, killing at least 7 and causing widespread power cuts across the country. On October 2, Ukraine claimed the first combat use of its domestically produced FP-7 ballistic missile against Russia, while Putin praised PM Modi's peace initiative and Ukraine sought to mend diplomatic ties with South Korea over North Korea tensions. On October 3, Russia launched strikes targeting Kyiv bridges, causing significant traffic disruption across the Ukrainian capital.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
